Reason Clauses: Using a Participle Clause and Because
There are different ways to construct a sentence with a reason clause. You should try to vary the way you construct sentences to make your English appear more dynamic.

I made mistakes because I was tired.
The team succeeded because she was the manager.

1. Participle clauses enable you to share information in a more economical way.
    Participle clauses can be formed with:
    the present participle (-ing form of the verb)
    Example: Being tired, I made mistakes.
    (It means that because the speaker was tired, mistakes were made.)
Crowds were waiting at the airport, hoping to see the CEO arrive.
Not feeling very well, James decided to leave for the day.
Being rather busy, I completely forgot the time.
Many managers take this step, but neglect to give their staff a sense of the big picture because they are caught up with the details.

1. Past participle
    This structure has a passive meaning.
    Example: Yelled at loudly, the dog sat down.
    (It means that someone was yelling at the dog.)

    To emphasize that one action took place before another, we can use a perfect participle (having + past participle).
    Example: Having lost my passport, I have to apply for a new one.
    The restaurant having closed, there was nowhere to eat.
You use an adverbial clause of time with a conjunction.

To talk about a complete action, you use the conjunction when to connect the time clause to the rest of the sentence.

For example:
When I arrived, the meeting was over.
We were discussing the issue when the manager walked in.

Example:
When you go to see her, she is always busy.
(In this case, when means that she is busy every time someone visits her.)
I walk to the office when it's nice out.
(When means that the speaker walks to the office every time it's nice out.)

images.text:
Grasping authority
 When you begin working in a managerial role, it's natural to want to be involved in all discussions and to feel the need to keep tabs on every move the team makes. Your team needs to know what your expectations are. You need to trust your team and step out of the way. Knowing the most effective way to distribute and complete the work, the team will likely perform well with some autonomy. When a team is provided with the resources and information it requires, it is able to work efficiently without you monitoring everything.

Defining roles
 As a manager, your responsibilities include overseeing the work of a team. Having many years experience in their careers, some team members are very knowledgeable. However, by no means should you adopt a laissez-faire attitude or approach in managing them. Adequate feedback, ongoing direction, good morale and motivation are things any good manager has to offer their team. Having outlined roles and responsibilities, you ensure your team understands their duties. Many managers know how to do this, but they fail to fill their staff in on the big picture because they are caught up in the details.
Learning to listen
 Those managers that are great at giving direction and providing feedback, are often the ones who neglect to ask for their team's ideas and input. Innovative ideas and new perspectives are resources that even junior staff can offer, and by not listening to them, you will miss out. When you launch a new project or consider a new process, hold a team brainstorming session.

Decision making
 Productivity in a business environment is impeded by indecisiveness or hesitation. Having gathered all the information you need, make a decision. Avoid procrastinating. When you make a decision take time to do research, or use tools available to you so that you can more easily choose a course of action to take.
Recognition and praise
When feedback is carefully delivered, it brings out the best in your team. Not giving your team praise when they succeed will make them feel undervalued. Praise is a simple way to make them feel appreciated. Also, praising the group or individuals during a meeting can really have a positive impact. Being committed to learning from your mistakes, you'll become more relaxed and confident in your role as manager.
